name: Undo instead of confirm
summary: For everyday actions that can be reversed, do them straight away and offer Undo, instead of asking 'Are you sure?' every time.
whenToUse: Archiving, removing from a list, marking done, moving to trash
Any capability with risk 'none' or 'low' that names an 'undo' capability
whenNotToUse: Actions that can't be reversed, or reverse only with loss: confirm-destructive
Moving money or sending on someone's behalf: confirm-destructive or review-and-submit
structure: Status (kind 'undo') says what happened, naming the thing
Its action is Undo, wired to the reversing capability

checks.description: An undo notice says what happened

journey.goal: Finish the action in one step, and recover from a slip in one step
journey.done: The action stands, or Undo restored it

agent: Carry out the action; if it was a mistake, activate Undo by its label.
sources: Raskin: The Humane Interface (undo over warnings)
NN/g: confirmation dialogs lose their power when overused
